open-question.question: Which store backs the cache?
open-question.recommendation: A crash mid-write is the one failure a cache must survive, and a transaction rules it out while the store stays one file.
open-question.alternative: Keep every entry in one SQLite database file beside the project. A transaction keeps a crashed write from corrupting the store. The store needs the sqlite3 module at run time.
Keep every entry in one JSON file rewritten whole on every change. The store is readable and diffable by hand. Every write rewrites the whole file, and a crash mid-write loses it.

open-question.question: How many times is a failed read retried before it is reported?
open-question.recommendation: Three retries ride out a transient fault without hiding a lasting one for long.
open-question.alternative: Retry a failed read three times, then report the last error. A transient fault is ridden out without the caller seeing it. A lasting fault is reported only after three more waits.
Report a failed read at once, retrying nothing. A fault reaches the caller with no delay. Every transient fault surfaces as an error.

open-question.question: How does the cache evict entries once it is full?
open-question.recommendation: With a flat JSON store every write already rewrites the whole file, so dropping it on overflow costs nothing a per-entry eviction would save.
open-question.alternative: Delete the whole store when it outgrows its limit and start empty. Eviction is one delete, with no bookkeeping per entry. Every warm entry is lost along with the cold ones.
Evict the entries read least recently until the store fits its limit again. Warm entries survive an eviction. Every read updates a recency stamp, which is one more write.
